Total (Location-Based) Emissions Intensity estimates the amount of emissions (carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, etc.) that the building produces per square foot over one year. Carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) is a general unit that combines the quantity and global warming potential of each greenhouse gas3. The envelope leakage tests (also known as “blower door tests”) were performed following the ASTM E779-19 Standard Test Method for Determining Air Leakage Rate by Fan Pressurization with adjustments for changes in air density due to temperature. Multi-Point air leakage tests were performed using TECTITE® 4.0 software, and TEC DG-1000® Digital Pressure and Flow Gauge micromanometer was used for pressure and airflow readings, and TEC Model 3 Fan®. As part of the test procedure, the interior hallways of the building were treated as the outside reference pressure.
